function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) – commonly known as **Ji‑sung Park** in Western contexts – is a retired South‑Korean professional footballer who is widely regarded as one of the most successful Korean players in European football history.

| Category | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Full name** | Park Ji‑sung (박지성) |
| **Date of birth** | 27 March 1981 |
| **Place of birth** | Seoul, South Korea |
| **Position** | Central / Defensive Midfielder (also played as a winger on occasion) |
| **Height** | 1.78 m (5 ft 10 in) |

### Club Career Highlights

| Years | Club | Appearances | Goals |
|-------|------|-------------|-------|
| 1999–2000 | Ulsan Hyundai (K League) | 30 | 4 |
| 2000–2004 | PSV Eindhoven (Eredivisie) | 112 | 12 |
| 2004–2015 | Manchester United (Premier League) | 292 | 12 |
| 2015–2016 | PSV Eindhoven (Eredivisie) | 28 | 1 |
| 2016–2017 | Ulsan Hyundai (K League) | 20 | 1 |
| 2017 | FC Seoul (K League) | 12 | 0 |

*Key achievements with Manchester United:*
- Premier League titles: 2006–07, 2007–08, 2008–09, 2010–11, 2012–13
- FA Cup: 2008–09, 2009–10, 2010–11
- UEFA Champions League runner‑up: 2007–08, 2008–09
- UEFA Europa League winner: 2016–17 (though he left before the final)

### International Career

- **South Korea National Team** (1999–2017) – 115 caps, 4 goals.
- Key tournaments: 2002 FIFA World Cup (semi‑finalist), 2004, 2007, 2010, 2014, 2018 FIFA World Cups, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 AFC Asian Cups.
- Notable moments: Scored the winning goal against the United States in the 2002 World Cup group stage; delivered a crucial assist in the 2006 World Cup against Italy.

### Playing Style & Reputation

- Known for his stamina, work‑rate, and ability to cover large areas of the pitch.
- Versatile: could play as a defensive midfielder, central midfielder, or even as a winger when needed.
- Praised for his tactical intelligence, passing accuracy, and leadership on the field.

### Post‑Retirement

- **Ambassadorial roles**: Served as a goodwill ambassador for the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia.
- **Coaching & Media**: Has appeared as a pundit on Korean sports networks and has expressed interest in coaching.
- **Philanthropy**: Involved in various charitable initiatives, including youth football development programs in South Korea.

### Fun Facts

- He was the first Korean player to win the Premier League title with Manchester United.
- His nickname among fans was “The Korean Messi” due to his dribbling and vision.
- He holds the record for the most appearances by a Korean player in the Premier League.

---

If you were referring to a different Ji Sung Park (e.g., a researcher, artist, or another public figure), let me know and I can provide information on that individual instead.
